Topics · Is the Quran from God?

What would it even mean for a book to be from God?

Not that God held a pen. The claim is about a message's source, in human language. What it says, and does not.

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَن يُكَلِّمَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا وَحْيًا أَوْ مِن وَرَآئِ حِجَابٍ أَوْ يُرْسِلَ رَسُولًا فَيُوحِىَ بِإِذْنِهِۦ مَا يَشَآءُ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ عَلِىٌّ حَكِيمٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And it is not for any human being that Allāh should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a partition or that He sends a messenger [i.e., angel] to reveal, by His permission, what He wills. Indeed, He is Most High and Wise.

Quran · Ash-Shura 42:51

Translation

which at the right time he will show, who is the blessed and only Ruler, the King of kings and Lord of lords. He alone has immortality, dwelling in unapproachable light, whom no man has seen nor can see, to whom be honor and eternal power. Amen.

Original · Ancient Greek

ἣν καιροῖς ἰδίοις δείξει ὁ μακάριος καὶ μόνος δυνάστης, ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν βασιλευόντων καὶ κύριος τῶν κυριευόντων, ὁ μόνος ἔχων ἀθανασίαν, φῶς οἰκῶν ἀπρόσιτον, ὃν εἶδεν οὐδεὶς ἀνθρώπων οὐδὲ ἰδεῖν δύναται· ᾧ τιμὴ καὶ κράτος αἰώνιον· ἀμήν.

1 Timothy · 6:15-16

World English Bible

﴿وَإِنَّهُۥ لَتَنزِيلُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ١٩٢ نَزَلَ بِهِ ٱلرُّوحُ ٱلْأَمِينُ١٩٣ عَلَىٰ قَلْبِكَ لِتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُنذِرِينَ١٩٤ بِلِسَانٍ عَرَبِىٍّ مُّبِينٍ١٩٥﴾

Translation of the meaning

And indeed, it [i.e., the Qur’ān] is the revelation of the Lord of the worlds. The Trustworthy Spirit [i.e., Gabriel] has brought it down Upon your heart, [O Muḥammad] - that you may be of the warners In a clear Arabic language.

Quran · Ash-Shu'ara 26:192-195

Translation

The angel answered him, “I am Gabriel, who stands in the presence of God. I was sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.

Original · Ancient Greek

καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ ἄγγελος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἐγώ εἰμι Γαβριὴλ ὁ παρεστηκὼς ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ ἀπεστάλην λαλῆσαι πρὸς σὲ καὶ εὐαγγελίσασθαί σοι ταῦτα·

the Gospel (Luke) · 1:19

World English Bible

Start by clearing away a picture. The claim is not that a book fell from the sky, or that God wrote with a hand. The claim is about source: that what is said begins with the Maker of all things and reaches people through a person. The first verse here says how, and it sets a limit first. God speaks to a human being in only three ways: by inspiration, from behind a veil, or through a messenger sent. No scene of God in a human place is offered.

A question for you

What picture did you have of a book from God, before reading this?

If you sayDictated word by word.
ThenThat is close to how Muslims understand it: the wording itself is held to be from God, carried faithfully. What is ruled out is the picture of God speaking in human form.
If you sayA person's inspired thoughts.
ThenThat is one way scripture is read. This book says the words are not its messenger's own. The third part looks at that.
If you sayI have never thought about it.
ThenThen you are starting with no picture to unlearn, which is a fine place to start.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا بِلِسَانِ قَوْمِهِۦ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمْ ۖ فَيُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِى مَن يَشَآءُ ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And We did not send any messenger except [speaking] in the language of his people to state clearly for them, and Allāh sends astray [thereby] whom He wills[649] and guides whom He wills. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

Translator's notes

[649] i.e., those who refuse His guidance.

Quran · Ibrahim 14:4

Why would a divine message be so human: in one language, with one people's images of camels and rain, addressing particular events? This verse gives the reason: every messenger is sent in the language of his people, to make things clear. A message that fits no people would reach none. So human language does not count against a divine source. It is what you would expect from a sender who wished to be understood. The fair objection is that you would also expect it from a human author.

A question for you

Does a book's human language count for or against a divine source, for you?

If you sayAgainst. It looks like any human book of its time.
ThenThat is the strongest form of the objection. Language alone cannot separate them, so you would need to look at something else.
If you sayFor. A message has to be understood.
ThenThen language is no objection for you. It is not yet evidence either.
If you sayNeither. It tells me nothing.
ThenThat may be the fairest view: it removes an objection and proves nothing.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَمَا يَنطِقُ عَنِ ٱلْهَوَىٰٓ٣ إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا وَحْىٌ يُوحَىٰ٤﴾

Translation of the meaning

Nor does he speak from [his own] inclination. It is not but a revelation revealed,

﴿كِتَـٰبٌ أَنزَلْنَـٰهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبَـٰرَكٌ لِّيَدَّبَّرُوٓا۟ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦ وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْأَلْبَـٰبِ﴾

Translation of the meaning

[This is] a blessed Book which We have revealed to you, [O Muḥammad], that they might reflect upon its verses and that those of understanding would be reminded.

Quran · Sad 38:29

Translation

Only be strong and very courageous. Be careful to observe to do according to all the law which Moses my servant commanded you. Don’t turn from it to the right hand or to the left, that you may have good success wherever you go. This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it; for then you shall make your way prosperous, and then you shall have good success. Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, for Yahweh your God is with you wherever you go.”

Original · Hebrew

רַק֩ חֲזַ֨ק וֶֽאֱמַ֜ץ מְאֹ֗ד לִשְׁמֹ֤ר לַעֲשׂוֹת֙ כְּכָל־הַתּוֹרָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר צִוְּךָ֙ מֹשֶׁ֣ה עַבְדִּ֔י אַל־תָּס֥וּר מִמֶּ֖נּוּ יָמִ֣ין וּשְׂמֹ֑אול לְמַ֣עַן תַּשְׂכִּ֔יל בְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר תֵּלֵֽךְ׃ לֹֽא־יָמ֡וּשׁ סֵפֶר֩ הַתּוֹרָ֨ה הַזֶּ֜ה מִפִּ֗יךָ וְהָגִ֤יתָ בּוֹ֙ יוֹמָ֣ם וָלַ֔יְלָה לְמַ֨עַן֙ תִּשְׁמֹ֣ר לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת כְּכָל־הַכָּת֖וּב בּ֑וֹ כִּי־אָ֛ז תַּצְלִ֥יחַ אֶת־דְּרָכֶ֖ךָ וְאָ֥ז תַּשְׂכִּֽיל׃ הֲל֤וֹא צִוִּיתִ֨יךָ֙ חֲזַ֣ק וֶאֱמָ֔ץ אַֽל־תַּעֲרֹ֖ץ וְאַל־תֵּחָ֑ת כִּ֤י עִמְּךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר תֵּלֵֽךְ׃

Joshua · 1:7-9

World English Bible

So what is the claim, in one line? The first lines here say the speaker does not speak from his own desire: it is a revelation given to him. That is a sharp claim. If true, the book is no expression of a man's culture or a community's hopes. It has an author who knows what the reader does not. It could correct its own messenger. It could be studied for ever without running out. And no one person's reading could contain it, not yours and not this app's.

A question for you

If a book really were from God, what would you expect to find in it?

If you sayNo mistakes.
ThenThat is the test the book sets itself: consistency. It can be examined.
If you sayThings I could not have worked out myself.
ThenThen you have named what revelation would add to reason, and that question has its own Step.
If you saySomething that knows me.
ThenThat is a test no one can run from outside, and it is real all the same. There is a way of looking into it.

The same in the other books
